headline: Canucks claim Cameron Crotty off waivers from Wild
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Canucks have claimed defenseman Cameron Crotty off waivers from the Wild, with the outlet noting Vancouver has lost 16 of its last 17 games after Monday's defeat to the Flyers. Crotty was drafted 82nd overall by the Coyotes in 2017 and put up 13 points in 64 AHL games for Tucson in 2022-23.

The number that matters here is Vancouver's. The Canucks are 3-16-1, and we have them at 39.9 percent of expected goals (the quality of chances, so a measure of who is creating the better looks). Their goalies are 14.8 goals worse than expected, so the record is partly a goaltending problem. Crotty won't fix that. In three games so far this season he has no points and logged 11.16 minutes a night, and his team took 49.22 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five while he was out there. Our model puts his expected goals at 0.13 per 60 minutes, which is a low-event, depth defender's profile. It's a small sample, but nothing in it suggests a player who moves Vancouver's numbers. We'd treat this as roster filler for a team that needs bodies, not a turning point.
